name: Sausage Hash Brown and Egg Casserole
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified 560 cal / 31g protein at the source, clears both bars with no adjustment, and it is only five ingredients, all board commodities. Make-ahead casserole is the single most meal-prep-native format on this list. Distinct from the sausage breakfast hash (bound custard casserole with hash browns and cheddar vs. roasted potato hash with cracked eggs), though the selector may want only one of the two breakfast bakes. | HARVEST:
OVERRIDE Italian Seasoning: CANON-MAPPER FIX: '2 lb hot breakfast sausage' mapped to Italian Seasoning (spice macros for 2 lb of sausage); -> Ground Pork at stated 2 lb
intro_html: Five ingredients, one baking dish, and it is arguably the most meal prep native recipe we have. Sausage, hash browns, cheddar and an egg custard baked until it sets into something you can cut into squares. Assemble it the night before if you want. It lands at {{protein}} grams of protein for about ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost).
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder): ~$0.13. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $24.57 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.76 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $33.38 across 14 servings, roughly $2.38 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $7.55 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $40.93. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a five ingredient casserole that reheats better than almost anything else in the library. Cut it into squares and the portioning is nearly done for you.
shop_smart: Ground pork seasoned at home beats bought breakfast sausage. The salt, pepper, garlic powder and onion powder are already in your cabinet, and you skip the markup on the pre seasoned tube.
Frozen hash browns are the second biggest line. The big bags are the better per ounce buy. Shredded and diced both work, so grab whichever is cheaper that week.
Buy a block of cheddar and shred it yourself. Pre shredded is coated in starch to keep it from clumping, which also keeps it from melting well. A block is usually cheaper and melts smoother.
Milk and eggs are the whole binder. Two of the cheapest items in the store are what hold this entire casserole together.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 350F and grease two large baking dishes.

Brown the ground pork in a skillet, breaking it into crumbles, seasoning as it cooks with the salt, black pepper, garlic powder and onion powder. Drain off the excess fat or the casserole will come out greasy.
Spread the frozen hash browns across the bottoms of the baking dishes. There is no need to thaw them first.
Scatter the cooked sausage over the hash browns, then most of the shredded cheddar over that.
Whisk the eggs and milk together with a little more salt and pepper until it is completely uniform, then pour it evenly over both dishes.
Top with the rest of the cheddar and bake until the center is set and no longer jiggles when you nudge the pan.
Let it rest at least ten minutes before you cut it. Cutting a hot casserole gets you a puddle instead of a square.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14, then cut the casserole into squares and adjust each container to hit that weight. Every bowl lands near {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.

steps: Brown and crumble the ground pork with salt, pepper, garlic powder and onion powder, then drain the fat.
Spread the frozen hash browns across two greased baking dishes.
Layer on the cooked sausage and most of the shredded cheddar.
Whisk the eggs and milk together and pour evenly over both dishes, then top with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 350F until the center is set, then rest before cutting.
